(The immediately preceding one-word "PLACEHOLDER" comment was an error of mine — an unset heredoc
path. Ignore it; the store is append-only so it cannot be removed. This is the intended content.)

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF THE PROPOSED DESIGN — 3 load-bearing pieces INVALIDATED. Change 1060 must NOT
be submitted as-is. Every finding below was re-verified by executing the code, not taken on the
reviewer's word.

F1 [CRITICAL — signed false PASS]. The compaction committed in 1060 DELETES WHOLE CHILD TICKETS on
an epic close and mislabels it as comment elision. Mechanism: an epic verifies with graph=True
(completion.py:352-353), so assemble_context concatenates one _format_ticket block PER TICKET, each
with its own "#### Comments" heading. _split_comment_block finds the FIRST such heading and treats
everything after it as droppable comment history — which is every child's header, description and
acceptance criteria. explicit_completion_criteria only parses the ROOT description, so child
criteria are never in the protected set. Reproduced directly:
    criteria the verifier will check: ['ROOT-AC1']
    CHILD-AC survived? False | child header survived? False
    marker emitted: "[... 7 earlier comment(s) elided ... they were NOT reviewed ...]"
A child whose AC is explicitly NOT done vanishes, the verifier checks only the root criteria, and
the gate can SIGN a PASS over unfinished work while telling the operator only that "comments" were
removed. This is the worst failure class this gate has.

F2 [HIGH]. The "whole comment entry" guarantee is false: _group_comment_entries starts a new entry
on any line beginning "- ", so markdown bullets INSIDE a comment body split it. A 2-comment ticket
grouped into 4 units; compaction can drop "AC-4 deliberately deferred" while keeping "AC-1..3
done", and the elided-count in the marker is wrong too.

F4 [HIGH — my safety rationale was BACKWARDS]. I argued request_limit = genuine-large-job (recover)
vs tool_calls_limit = stuck-loop (do not recover). But runner.py:414-417 sets
request_limit = ceil(max_iter/2) and tool_calls_limit = max(8, max_iter) — verified as 240 vs 480
at the default. A classic runaway (one tool call per model turn) therefore trips request_limit
FIRST and never reaches tool_calls_limit, so the discriminant admits exactly the case it was meant
to exclude. The step-budget signal does NOT reliably separate a runaway from a big job.

F7 [MEDIUM]. Units error: sizing.container_budget returns TOKENS (868,000 for a 1M window) and the
plan used it as a CHARACTER budget. Also sizing.largest_window_tokens returns 1,000,000 for haiku,
sonnet, opus AND an unknown model alike, so the AC "changing the configured model changes the
derived budget" is unsatisfiable via that API.

F9 [HIGH — the next false-block]. _EVIDENCE_CHARS = 12,000 per criterion vs
_MAX_TOTAL_EVIDENCE_CHARS = 96,000 aggregate is incoherent above 8 criteria (96,000/14 = 6,857 mean
for 9fd4) — the SAME bound-vs-bound incoherence this ticket condemns for criteria-vs-context. Worse,
the aggregate check runs INSIDE the loop AFTER each billable call, so a 14-criterion ticket pays for
all 14 evidence calls and then hard-fails with no verdict.

F10 [HIGH]. per_criterion_steps was never stated, and the plan's own figure (~34/criterion) yields
max(480, 14 x 34) is approximately 480 — the budget that already failed. The AC "9fd4 closes at
DEFAULT settings" is not supported by the plan's own arithmetic; roughly 70-100 steps per criterion
is needed for real headroom (9fd4 spent ~780s over 240 model requests, about 3.25s each).

F11. No wall-clock deadline exists anywhere (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S is per-request only; no SIGALRM or
deadline in the LLM path), so step scaling is NOT neutered by a timeout — but a 30-criterion ticket
at 70 steps/criterion implies roughly 57 minutes of a blocking close with no progress output.

CONSEQUENCE — the design changes. Compaction is subtle, dangerous, and (once the budget is raised)
nearly worthless. The safer design is to DROP compaction entirely: raise the budget so real tickets
fit (9fd4 is 34,282 chars; db1c's 2932 is 41,595 — a 400,000-char budget covers ~10x the worst
observed), and above it refuse with an accurate, actionable message. A refusal is a VISIBLE
false-block; a bad elision is an INVISIBLE signed false PASS, and for a signing gate that trade is
clear. Likewise F4 means the entry predicate should stop trying to classify the failure and instead
rely on recovery's own BOUNDED blast radius (per-criterion calls capped at 40 iterations),
excluding only LLMUnavailableError (the model cannot run at all) and CompletionRecoveryError (do
not nest recovery inside its own handler). F9's evidence bounds must come into scope or 9fd4 still
will not close.
